mission.title: envoy: Accessing request headers in envoy_on_response (lua HTTP filter).
mission.description: Accessing request headers in envoy_on_response (lua HTTP filter).. Requested by 17+ users.

steps.title: Check current envoy deployment
steps.description:
Verify your envoy version and configuration:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n envoy -l app.kubernetes.io/name=envoy
helm list -n envoy 2>/dev/null || echo "Not installed via Helm"
```
This feature requires a working envoy installation.

steps.title: Review envoy configuration
steps.description:
Inspect the relevant envoy configuration:
```bash
kubectl get all -n envoy -l app.kubernetes.io/name=envoy
kubectl get configmap -n envoy -l app.kubernetes.io/part-of=envoy
```
I'm trying to use a [lua HTTP filter](https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/configuration/http_filters/lua_filter) to set a response header whose value depends on a request header.

steps.title: Apply the fix for Accessing request headers in envoy_on_response (lua HTTP…
steps.description:
Commit Message: lua: add `requestHeaders()` accessor for response path
Additional Description: Adds `requestHeaders()` to the response handle so `envoy_on_response` can read what the request carried. Today the only routes from request to response are dynamic metadata and filter state, both of which
```yaml
- name: envoy.filters.http.lua
            typed_config:
              "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.config.filter.http.lua.v2.Lua
              inline_code: |
                function envoy_on_request(request_handle)
                  request_handle:streamInfo():dynamicMetadata():set("context", "foo", "bar")
                end
                function envoy_on_response(response_handle)
                  local foo = response_handle:streamInfo():dynamicMetadata():get("context")["foo"]
                  response_handle:logInfo(foo)
                end
```

steps.title: Verify the feature works
steps.description:
Test that the new capability is working as expected:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n envoy -l app.kubernetes.io/name=envoy
kubectl get events -n envoy --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | tail -10
```
Confirm the feature described in "Accessing request headers in envoy_on_response (lua HTTP…" is functioning correctly.

resolution.summary:
Commit Message: lua: add `requestHeaders()` accessor for response path
Additional Description: Adds `requestHeaders()` to the response handle so `envoy_on_response` can read what the request carried. Today the only routes from request to response are dynamic metadata and filter state, both of which cost a serialisation per request.

The returned handle is writable.

                end
                function envoy_on_response(response_handle)
                  local foo = response_handle:streamInfo():dynamicMetadata():get("context")["foo"]
                  response_handle:logInfo(foo)
                end

name: envoy.lua
        typed_config:
          "@type": "type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.lua.v3.Lua"
          inlineCode: |
            function envoy_on_request(request_handle)
              request_handle:streamInfo():dynamicMetadata():set("context","bar ", "foo")
            end
            function envoy_on_response(response_handle)
              local val = response_handle:streamInfo():dynamicMetadata():get("context")["foo"]
              response_handle:headers():add("x-custom-header", val)
            end

function envoy_on_request(request_handle)
                local request_headers = request_handle:headers()
                local headers = {}
                for key, value in pairs(request_headers) do
                  headers[key] = value
                end
                request_handle:streamInfo():dynamicMetadata():set("context", "request.info", headers)
              end

              function envoy_on_response(response_handle)
                local request_headers = response_handle:streamInfo():dynamicMetadata():get("context")["request.info"]
                local response_headers = response_handle:headers()
